name: Hoehn and Yahr Staging of Parkinson's Disease

version.label: Original Hoehn and Yahr (1967), stages 1–5
version.detail: The 'modified' version with stages 1.5 and 2.5 is not combined; the MDS Task Force (2004) recommends the original scale.

purpose: Describes the stage of motor disability in Parkinson's disease.

options.label: Stage 1: Unilateral involvement only, usually with minimal or no functional disability
Stage 2: Bilateral or midline involvement without impairment of balance
Stage 3: Bilateral disease: mild to moderate disability with impaired postural reflexes; physically independent
Stage 4: Severely disabling disease; still able to walk or stand unassisted
Stage 5: Confinement to bed or wheelchair unless aided

clinicalContext.text: A simple global staging used in clinical description and trial eligibility (e.g. for deep brain stimulation selection).

clinicalInsights.text: Record whether the patient was assessed 'on' or 'off' medication.

limitations.text: Weighted to motor and postural impairment; non-motor symptoms are not captured.

guideSections.what: Five stages from unilateral disease to wheelchair or bed bound.
guideSections.howToPerform: Assess laterality, balance (pull test) and independence; choose the stage.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Used with MDS-UPDRS and functional assessment.
